newsitem.title: UK: Horlick says to meet Deutsche Bank board.
newsitem.headline: Horlick says to meet Deutsche Bank board.

text.p: Nicola Horlick, former head of British pension fund business at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, said on Friday she would travel to Frankfurt to meet the management board of Deutsche Bank.

Horlick told the BBC's "Working Lunch" television programme that she had requested the meeting, adding that allegations she had tried to get a job with a rival firm, which led to her suspension earlier this week, were "absolutely untrue", and that she had received "very unfair treatment" from MGAM.

The high-flying Horlick, speaking by telephone from the departure lounge at London's Heathrow airport, repeated her assertion that she had been "constructively dismissed" by the asset management company and this had forced her resignation.

Horlick said she had no wish to leave MGAM. "I like doing what I'm doing, I'm keen to stick with my team," she said, adding other potential employers were waiting to speak to her but that she was concentrating on sorting out the MGAM debacle.
Horlick's resignation came as it emerged she had been offered and accepted the position of managing director of MGAM just days before her suspension.

The mother of five children, Horlick is said to have earned one million pounds ($1.67 million) a year and her advisers have said that if her departure is confirmed, she will attempt to recover money from MGAM which she claims is due to her. ($1=.5979 Pound)
